reason: At base the JIT fastpass only guards the issues concat with the presence check, so safeParse({}) succeeds but leaks {a:'leaked'} into the output, violating the expectation of no key.

At head the generated branch guards both issues and assignment on !issues.length || present, so an absent optional key with a failing check yields success with no key, and a present failing key still fails.
At base the paragraph continuation lookahead only treats spaces-only lines as blank, so a tab-only separator line is absorbed and the two lines merge into one paragraph instead of two.

At head the lookahead is widened to [ \t]+\n so a tab-only line counts as blank and separates the paragraphs, producing two distinct

elements as expected.
The PR only hardens the error-path stack decoration in Axios.request's catch handler; the success path and default JSON response parsing into an object are untouched, so the behavior holds at base.
The change only affects error decoration in the catch handler; default JSON parsing of successful response bodies is unchanged at head, so data remains a parsed object.
Parsing a simple boolean flag is unrelated to the negative-number regex change; the flag is recognized and set to true at base.
The regex change only affects negative-number detection; boolean flag parsing is unaffected at head, so the flag reads true with no error.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt goes straight to JsonPrimitive.getAsInt/Integer.parseInt, which accepts full-width Unicode digits and silently yields 123 instead of raising a parsing error.
At head nextInt validates STRING tokens with validateAscii and throws MalformedJsonException for non-ASCII characters, so the full-width digits are rejected as expected.
At base parseSearchPath uses the alphanumeric-only regex /[a-zA-z0-9$]{1,}/, so 'test-db' is split into 'test' and 'db' and the SQL sets two schemas instead of one.
At head the regex is a delimiter blocklist /[^\s,"\']+/ so 'test-db' matches as a single segment and the SQL becomes set search_path to "test-db".
The PR only reworks ByteBufferUtil.fromStream buffer recycling on exceptions; Glide's transformation eligibility for requests without dontTransform is untouched, so the behavior holds at base.
The buffer-leak fix does not touch request options or transformation application, so configured transformations still apply at head.
At base allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics is a computed union of allowed symbols and alphanumerics, so an identifier using only a configured allowed symbol passes the naming rule.

At head the union is cached but refreshed via didSet when allowed_symbols is applied (and in the initializer per the description), with reported verification showing identical lint results, so the allowed-symbol identifier still passes.

The PR only adds a <cstdint> include for GCC 15 compilation and cannot affect image loading; node-canvas decodes percent-encoded data URI octets before parsing the SVG payload, so the image loads at base as well.
Arrow's shift adds real elapsed time: 2025-03-08T18:30-06:00 plus 10h is 2025-03-09T10:30 UTC, which is 05:30 at the post-spring-forward -05:00 offset; the Afrikaans locale PR is unrelated.
The GCC 15 header include is compile-time only and cannot change image loading; percent-encoded data URI octets are decoded before SVG parsing at head, so the image loads.

The PR only changes Cookie header directive parsing, which is unrelated to content decoding; Vapor's URL-encoded form decoder yields all-nil optionals for an empty body at base, so the handler responds normally.
Cookie header parsing is unrelated to form decoding; at head an empty form-urlencoded body still decodes into the all-optional type with nil fields rather than a 422.
The PR only fixes spelling in a test and a comment; Afero's in-memory Remove rejects non-empty directories with a directory-not-empty error and leaves the contents intact at base.
Spelling-only changes cannot affect filesystem semantics; at head Remove on a non-empty directory still returns the not-empty error and preserves /dirname.
The PR only corrects a json_encode call in a JSON type test, unrelated to schema comparison; the Comparator handles multiple equally-matching rename candidates and completes without warnings at base.
The test-only JSON flag fix does not touch the Comparator; schema comparison with two equivalent added indexes still completes cleanly at head.
Arrow shift adds elapsed time: 2025-03-08T18:30-06:00 plus 10h lands at 2025-03-09T10:30 UTC, i.e. 05:30 at the post-transition -05:00 offset; the Afrikaans locale PR does not affect this.

The PR only touches CircuitBreakerStateMachine predicate evaluation, unrelated to the rate limiter; the semaphore-based rate limiter's scheduled refresh keeps replenishing permits up to the lowered limit at base.
The circuit-breaker permit-leak fix does not affect RateLimiter; at head the refresh task continues after changeLimitForPeriod(1) and admits calls at the new rate.

The PR only affects prefer-template's ASI handling; no-var's autofix skips converting a var that is referenced before its declaration (preserving hoisting), so the fixed script still prints undefined at base.

prefer-template semicolon insertion is unrelated to no-var; at head no-var still leaves the hoisted var unconverted when it is used before its initializer, so the script prints undefined without a TDZ error.
The PR only changes logformatter_adapter log-call shaping, unrelated to JOBDIR persistence; Scrapy's scheduler/dupefilter persistence lets a SitemapSpider resume remaining sitemap URLs at base.
Log formatting changes cannot affect crawl resumption; at head the restarted spider continues crawling remaining sitemap pages instead of closing immediately.

The PR only widens --sanitize bidi detection, unrelated to width/wrapping; the capacity-overflow panic at --terminal-width=1 is already fixed in the base per the CHANGELOG, so bat clamps the highlight background and exits 0.
The sanitize change cannot affect rendering; at head bat handles a full-width line wider than the 1-column terminal without panicking and exits 0.
The PR only optimizes the RFC5424 structured-data regex, unrelated to the file output plugin; each chunk in a multi-key batch is written and its per-key symlink created at base.
Syslog parser regex changes cannot affect out_file symlinks; at head a follow-up record for a previously-seen key updates that key's symlink as expected.

The PR only changes ConcurrentBag handoff spinning for virtual threads; HikariCP generates pool names via an atomic counter without touching System.getProperties, so construction does not block on the system-properties lock at base.
Virtual-thread spin changes are unrelated to pool-name generation; at head concurrent unnamed pool creation completes without deadlocking on the shared properties object.
The PR only fixes SORT ACL key extraction, unrelated to RDB persistence; BGSAVE of a few-megabyte dataset on a 32-bit Redis build completes successfully at base.
ACL key-spec parsing cannot affect background saving; at head the save-point-triggered BGSAVE on a 32-bit host terminates successfully.

The PR only fixes globaldir/CWD bookkeeping during window context switches, unrelated to CTRL-A number handling; Neovim's addsub preserves all digits of an over-64-bit decimal when incrementing at base.
The cwd fix cannot affect CTRL-X arithmetic; at head decrementing the 50-digit number yields the exact minus-one value with all digits intact.
The PR only reworks external file cache block reclamation, unrelated to operator binding; DuckDB resolves [1] || NULL to list concatenation, yielding an INTEGER[] typed NULL at base.
File-cache changes cannot affect type resolution; at head both || and list_concat report the same INTEGER[] type for a list concatenated with NULL.
The PR only reworks ScrollBar touch drag input handling; Godot emits NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE before freeing while the object is still valid, so the GDScript override reads its member safely at base.
ScrollBar input changes are unrelated to reference counting; at head releasing the last reference runs the PREDELETE handler on a valid object without crashing.

The PR only adds a ValueError for categorical features with absolute_error in trees, unrelated to feature_selection; f_regression returns F=0.0 and p=1.0 for a constant column without NaN or sqrt warnings at base.
Tree categorical validation cannot affect correlation computation; at head r_regression returns a finite correlation for a near-constant column with no RuntimeWarning.
The PR only fixes the swagger-ui readonly attribute in the UI, unrelated to vault-agent; the file sink applies the configured octal mode 0640 to the token file at base.
UI field handling cannot affect the agent's sink writer; at head the token file is created with permission bits 600 as configured.

At base write_usage with empty args goes through wrap_text('', initial_indent=prefix) which returns '', so a command with no parameters renders a blank usage line instead of 'Usage: cli' (issue #3360).
At head write_usage short-circuits when args is empty and writes the prefix plus program name with the trailing space stripped, so the first help line is exactly 'Usage: cli'.
The PR only changes IPv6 host parsing in app.run and session_transaction; Flask's default JSON provider already serializes dict return values as compact application/json responses at base.
IPv6 parsing fixes do not touch response serialization; at head a dict-returning view still yields application/json with compact encoding.
The PR only changes deprecated-alias lookup to id-based for unhashable types; pydantic's core required-field validation raises a missing-field error at base regardless.
The alias-lookup change does not affect field requirements; at head omitting a required field still raises a validation error identifying it as missing.
logging.WARN is an alias of logging.WARNING (same value 30), so the default WARN level already suppresses INFO SQL records with echo off and logs them with echo on at base.
The rename to logging.WARNING is value-identical; at head the effective level still blocks info-level SQL when echo is off and logs statements when echo is on.

Once attribute methods are generated, both the real column and the aliased computed attribute are read through generated methods, so the access ratio stays well under 20x at base; the thread-safety rework only changes the method_missing fallback.
At head steady-state reads of the computed alias still hit the generated attribute method rather than the heavier method_missing path, keeping the ratio far below the 20x threshold.
At base each dispatch creates a fresh WrappedListener stored in the callStack, so getCalledListeners iterates two distinct entries after two dispatches of the same listener.
At head postProcess deduplicates by original listener per event (in_array check before appending to calledListenerInfos), so two dispatches of the same listener yield only one entry instead of two.
Subcommand scoping of dynamic completions depends on the generated command-tracking logic, which the shellcheck cleanup does not touch, so each hook still sees the correct current command at base.

The COMPREPLY population change (while-read instead of word-splitting assignment) is functionally equivalent since bash resets COMPREPLY per completion; the current-command routing is unchanged at head.
Express's extended query parser uses qs with the default arrayLimit of 100, so 25 repeated 'ids' keys parse to a 25-element array at base (qs 6.13.0).
Bumping qs to 6.14.0 does not change repeated-key array parsing for 25 values under the default arrayLimit, so the result remains an ordered array at head.
At base get_environ_proxies has the single-parameter signature def get_environ_proxies(url), so calling it with only a URL succeeds and returns the proxy dict.
At head the signature becomes get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy) with no default for no_proxy, so calling it with only the URL raises a TypeError for the missing required argument.
At base parse_unit_value rejects '.foons' immediately (first byte is not a digit), so the bare word falls through to string parsing and [.foons] yields '.foons'.
At head '.foons' enters parse_unit_value via the new '.' allowance, but 'foons' is not a valid unit and '.' is not a number, so it returns None and the value still parses as the string '.foons'.

At base CurlFactory always attaches a sink (CURLOPT_FILE/WRITEFUNCTION) even for HEAD requests, which with an Accept-Encoding header makes the cURL transfer fail (guzzle issue #2741), so the HEAD request errors instead of completing.

At head applyHandlerOptions skips sink wiring entirely when the method is HEAD, so no write callback conflicts with the NOBODY response and the HEAD request with Accept-Encoding completes with a valid status.

For a match (=) assertion ExUnit's diff uses the :match context where maybe_escape returns the value unescaped and it is simply inspected, so the improper list [1 | 2] renders fine and the failure is a clean 'match (=) failed' at base.
The new map-escaping clause only applies outside the :match context, so at head the match failure for :foo = %{bar: [1 | 2]} is still formatted by inspection without crashing.

At base css_props registers a teardown that calls element.remove(), so when the dynamic component re-renders the element carrying the scoped custom property is removed and the inner component loses the red --prop color (issue #16115).

At head the element-removal teardown is deleted and dynamic Component css_props are compiled through the same $.component path, so the custom property survives the toggle and the color stays red without hydration errors.

At base the handler gates on code.includes('new URL') and the assetImportMetaUrlRE uses \s* between parts, which spans newlines, so a multi-line new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url) is matched, resolved and emitted as an asset.

At head the new transform code filter /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ lacks the s flag, so .+ cannot span the newlines of a multi-line new URL(...) call; the handler is skipped entirely and the asset is never bundled.
At base no FZF_CURRENT_ITEM is exported, so a NUL-delimited item puts no NUL byte into the child environment and the preview command starts and prints ok.

At head environImpl appends FZF_CURRENT_ITEM=item.AsString(), which for a NUL-delimited item embeds a NUL byte in the environment; Go cannot pass a NUL in an env value to the child, so starting the preview fails.

At base switching to edgeToEdge falls through to setSystemUiVisibility(LAYOUT_STABLE|LAYOUT_HIDE_NAVIGATION|LAYOUT_FULLSCREEN), which replaces the visibility and clears the immersiveSticky HIDE_NAVIGATION/FULLSCREEN flags, so the bars reappear.

At head the edgeToEdge branch calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) and returns without any setSystemUiVisibility call, so the HIDE_NAVIGATION/FULLSCREEN flags set by the prior immersiveSticky mode are never cleared and the bars stay hidden.

At base the MultipleCaseAssignment semantic check does not exist yet, and no other preview check flags the refutable class pattern, so 'case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes)' reports no syntax error.

At head the new visitor inserts keyword.attr into the same name set and then visits the keyword's capture pattern, so for ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) the name 'num_classes' is inserted twice and a spurious MultipleCaseAssignment syntax error is reported.
At base the non-pointer branch calls sli.Index(i) without growing the slice, so the second block (i=1) against a length-1 slice panics with index out of range instead of decoding two entries.
At head the decoder appends a fresh zero value when i >= sli.Len(), so both blocks decode into a two-element slice with the placeholder overwritten and no panic.
At base the mock only calls setTimezone when an explicit timezone was passed, so Carbon::now() without a timezone returns the test instant still in America/Los_Angeles instead of the UTC default.
At head the mocked instance is converted to $timezone ?? date_default_timezone_get(), so reading now() without a timezone presents the reference moment in UTC, matching the expected representation.

At base PROTOCOL_RELATIVE_REGEX is /^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+/, which needs exactly two leading slashes immediately followed by a non-slash, so '///test.com', '/\t//test.com' and '/\\/test.com' all fail to match and are not classified protocol-relative.
At head the regex /^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\]/ accepts two or more slashes with optional whitespace between them and mixed slash directions, so all three inputs are classified protocol-relative.
The PR only swaps asBytes() for getBytesInternal() in hash-combining helpers; Guava's Hashing.md5().hashString("abc", UTF_8) produces the canonical 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72 digest at base.
The copy-avoiding accessor change does not alter produced values; at head MD5 of 'abc' still yields 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72.
The PR only relocates unchanged diagnostic descriptors; Refit's source generator already produces a working GET client method for a valid [Get] interface at base.

Moving RF001/RF002 descriptors into DiagnosticDescriptors with identical codes and severities changes nothing about stub generation; at head the generated client still issues the expected GET request.
The PR only deletes loop-final continue statements with no control-flow change, and a plain HTTP/1.1 GET with Content-Length body already works at base, returning 200 and the exact body.
Removing redundant continues (each already the last action of its loop branch) leaves behavior identical; at head the fresh HTTP/1.1 request still yields 200 with the full expected body.
At base to_iso8601/2 for a non-ISO calendar converts to Calendar.ISO and then calls to_iso8601/1, discarding :basic, so the call returns '2001-01-01' instead of the expected '20010101'.
At head the converted ISO date is passed through to_iso8601(format), so the Holocene date renders as '2001-01-01' by default and '20010101' with :basic.
At base setEndDate updates the internal endDate but never resynchronizes the engine-managed native DatePeriod properties on PHP 8.2+, so $period->end still reports the original 2024-09-30.
At head setEndDate calls syncNativePeriod(), which re-runs parent::__construct with the new endDate, so both ->end and getEndDate() report 2025-06-15 00:00:00.
At base headline builds the request line with no whitespace validation, so with a pass-through normalizer a path containing a newline is transmitted rather than rejected with an invalid-URI error.
At head headline raises RequestError 'Invalid request URI' when the resolved request URI matches /\s/, so the newline-containing path is refused before anything is sent.
The PR only adds a pluralName to the Albanian locale's million entry; the default English number-to-words already renders 1000000 as 'one million' and 2000000 as 'two million' at base.
Albanian locale data changes cannot affect English output; at head the English conversions still return 'one million' and 'two million'.
The PR only changes how environment Properties are copied into the property registry; Koin's singleton scope already caches and returns the same instance on repeated resolves at base.
Filtering non-string property keys does not touch instance resolution; at head two resolves of a singleton definition still return the identical instance.
At base replaceElement appends the new key, swaps it into position 1 and removes the old one, yielding (a,1),(z,2),(c,3), and the duplicate-key attempt trips the 'Duplicate key' precondition.
At head the same append/swap/removeLast steps are factored into OrderedSet._replaceNew with identical semantics, so the replace and the duplicate-key precondition behave exactly as before.
At base parseSizeInBytes parses '-5' from '-5MB' and explicitly clamps negative sizes to 0 before multiplying, so the accessor returns 0.
At head max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is value-identical to the old if-clamp, so '-5MB' still yields 0 bytes.

At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec takes n.children[0] under wildChild, but with both /prefix/xxx and /prefix/:id registered children[0] is the static node, so the nType switch hits the default case and panics ('invalid node type') instead of redirecting or returning 404.

At head the lookup first tries static children via indices and only then falls back to the wildcard child at children[len-1], so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to /prefix/xxx and /prefix/a/b/c cleanly returns not-found.
At base toBigInt returns the nil Int unchanged when Exp is 0 and Int64Value then dereferences it via IsInt64, so Numeric{Valid:true}.Int64Value() panics instead of returning zero.
At head toBigInt short-circuits a nil Int to big.NewInt(0), so Int64Value succeeds with 0, consistent with Float64Value.
The PR only changes tab-stop handling in the renderer; bubbletea's Quit is safe to call from another goroutine and already terminates the run loop cleanly at base.
Tab-stop restoration cannot affect the quit channel; at head an external Quit still makes Run return promptly without error.

At base run_until_cancelled always builds and polls RunUntilCancelledFuture, which polls the wrapped future even when the token is already cancelled, so the panicking future is started instead of resolving to Ready(None).
At head run_until_cancelled checks self.is_cancelled() first and returns None without ever constructing or polling the wrapped future, so one poll yields Ready(None) with no panic.
The PR only avoids loading ignore files for skipped/max-depth directories in the serial walker; case-insensitive matching is handled by the regex engine and works at base.
Walker ignore-file loading changes do not affect pattern matching; at head a case-insensitive search still reports all occurrences regardless of case.
serde_derive already sets Default::Default for skip_deserializing fields when no container default exists, so the omitted skipped field deserializes to its type's default at base.
The refactor collapses two nested ifs into an equivalent is_none() && is_some() condition with identical semantics, so skipped fields still get their type default at head.
